turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I've popped him in room two. Observations are done, blood pressure one forty-eight over eighty-six, pulse seventy-eight, temperature thirty-six point eight, oxygen ninety-eight percent on air.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lovely, thanks. Not feverish on that, which is something. I'll call him.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Come on then, love. Mind the step.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Dr Shah. What's going on with you?
[SEG0005] person_4 (PATIENT): Toe.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His big toe, the right one. It came up last night and he can barely put the foot down.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since last night, right big toe. How bad is the pain, if ten is the worst?
[SEG0008] person_4 (PATIENT): Nine.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nine, so properly severe. Swollen with it, or just sore?
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Swollen. And red. He wouldn't let me near it this morning.
[SEG0011] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever, shivers, feeling rotten in yourself?
[SEG0013] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): And any pain in the knees, the ankles, the other toe?
[SEG0015] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ever had this before?
[SEG0017] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): When, roughly?
[SEG0019] person_4 (PATIENT): Year.
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): About a year back. Same toe, same carry-on. It settled after a few days and he never came in, typical.

[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thinking aloud, a big toe that blows up red and painful overnight, and the same a year ago, that is the classic gout pattern, uric acid crystals in the joint. Did you knock it or twist it?
[SEG0022] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, no injury then. What tablets are you on at home?
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Only the water tablet. Bendroflumethiazide, two and a half milligrams, every morning, for his blood pressure.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Bendroflumethiazide, yes, and thiazides can nudge the uric acid up, which rather fits. Are you actually taking it every morning?
[SEG0026] person_4 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): You suppose. So I can't be sure it's every day. We'll leave the tablet as it is for the moment. Do you drink?
[SEG0028] person_4 (PATIENT): Beer.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): How often, though?
[SEG0030] person_4 (PATIENT): Weekends.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A few pints, Saturday and Sunday. Nothing in the week, I'll give him that.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weekends only. Beer is a very common trigger for this. Let me look at that toe.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): The right first metatarsophalangeal joint is hot, red and swollen, and exquisitely tender to touch. The skin is intact, no break and no pus.
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh, wait. You kicked the chair last night, didn't you, getting up?
[SEG0035] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): You did? You told me there was no injury.
[SEG0037] person_4 (PATIENT): Chair.
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The leg of the kitchen chair. He yelped, and then the toe blew up after that.

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): So there was a knock, which muddies things. Gout still sits at the top of my list, but I can't fully set aside straightforward trauma from the chair. Infection looks unlikely, mind, with a normal temperature and the skin unbroken.

[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm going to start colchicine, five hundred micrograms twice a day by mouth, for three days. If the colchicine upsets your stomach, we can switch to naproxen, five hundred milligrams twice a day with food, but only if that happens.
[SEG0041] person_4 (PATIENT): Fine.

[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll also send a blood test for the uric acid. It can sit in the normal range right in the middle of an attack, so it won't prove or disprove this on its own, but it's still worth having.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): I can take the bloods now, before you go, if that suits.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes please. Serum uric acid today.
[SEG0045] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should he lay off the beer, then?
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd ease off the beer this weekend at least, while it's angry. Keep the foot up, ice it if you can bear it, and don't poke at it.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back if it isn't settling in three days, or sooner if you get a fever or the redness starts spreading. The nurse will take that blood now.

omissions.text: There was an initial denial of injury/knock, later corrected when the patient and family confirmed he kicked the leg of a kitchen chair last night; the doctor explicitly noted this contradiction/disagreement.
Doctor advised to leave bendroflumethiazide as it is for the moment.
Doctor said thiazides can raise uric acid, fitting the suspected gout.
Doctor considered infection unlikely because temperature was normal and the skin was unbroken.
Doctor explained that serum uric acid can be normal during an acute attack, so the test will not prove or disprove gout on its own.
